newsitem.title: USA: Goldman Sachs says posts strong Q4, 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: Goldman Sachs says posts strong Q4, 1996 profits.

text.p: Goldman Sachs & Co said fiscal 1996 was the second best year in the investment bank's history, with pre-tax profits jumping to $2.6 billion compared to $1.37 billion in fiscal 1995.

Goldman said revenues for the year jumped 37 percent to $6.14 billion from 1995's $4.48 billion. Expenses were $3.53 billion for the year compared to $3.11 billion last year and headcount was near 9,000 compared to 8,200 employees in 1995. Capital is now about $5.25 billion, the firm said.
The fourth quarter was the firm's third best quarter ever, the investment bank said.

For the fiscal fourth quarter, the firm earned $743 million on a pre-tax basis, up 68 percent compared to the $440 million earned last year. Revenues for the quarter were $1.54 billion compared to $1.3 billion last year and expenses were $790 million compared to $860 million last year.

In a statement, Goldman chief financial officer John Thain said, "Fourth quarter performance was very strong with all divisions contributing across the board to profitable results for the quarter and for the year."
